title: RSS checkpoint advances past failed article processing

evidence.quote:
val processed = contentProcessor.processWithRssContent(
                url = link,
                rssContent = item.content,
                rssDescription = item.description,
                rssTitle = item.title,
                rssAuthor = item.author,
                minWordCount = minWordCount
            ) ?: run {
                errorCount++
                return@mapNotNull null
            }

reasoning: When a feed returns multiple new RSS items and at least one succeeds, the repository stores the current wall-clock time as lastFetched even if other items in the same batch failed content processing. On the next onlyNew run, those failed items are older than the new checkpoint and are not retried.
reproduction: Have fetchNewArticles return two items newer than the old lastFetched; make processWithRssContent return an article for the first and null for the second. The method updates lastFetched to now, causing the failed second item to be skipped by future onlyNew fetches.
recommendation: Advance the checkpoint only to a safe per-item timestamp, such as the newest successfully processed item before the first failure, or track seen/failed article IDs separately so transient processing failures can be retried without reprocessing successful items.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No ArticleRepository tests were linked or found in app/src/test for mixed success/failure checkpoint behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that simulates one successful and one failed RSS item and asserts the feed checkpoint does not advance beyond the failed item's publish timestamp or that the failed item remains retryable.
minimumFixScope: ArticleRepository.fetchArticles checkpoint update logic and, if needed, the feed lastFetched persistence contract.
